question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.text: tend to underestimate the cumulative health burden the framework predicts at the population level.
be unable to detect any health disparity at all in the population they study.
find that the single level they focus on accounts for nearly all of the observed disparity in their data.
show that institutionalized racism is the single most important driver of measurable health outcomes.

explanation: The correct answer is A. The passage gives two premises: the framework distinguishes three levels at which racism acts on health, each leaving distinct traces, and all three act on the same population at the same time. If the levels are simultaneous and additive, a study sensitive to only one of them captures that level's contribution but misses the other two, so it will tend to underestimate the cumulative burden the framework predicts. A states that measured conclusion. C reverses it, since one instrument cannot capture nearly the whole effect when three levels contribute. B overstates the case: such a study would still detect the disparity from the level it measures, so the issue is magnitude, not invisibility. D singles out one level as dominant, which the passage explicitly declines to do.

_meta.anchor: Camara Phyllis Jones — social epidemiologist; three-level framework of racism and health

passage: Social epidemiologist Camara Phyllis Jones argues that population-health research improves when its frameworks are made measurable. She distinguishes three levels at which racism can act on health: institutionalized (unevenly distributed rules and resources), personally mediated (differential treatment in everyday encounters), and internalized (the absorption of negative beliefs about one's own group). Each level, she notes, leaves distinct traces in survey and administrative data, so each can be tracked by indicators specific to it. Because all three levels act on the same population at the same time, her framework implies that researchers who collect data sensitive to only one of the three will ______
